skill.name: sharepoint-audit
skill.description: Guides a local SharePoint Online permission audit using PowerShell, Python, certificate authentication, and generated Markdown or HTML reports.
skill.summary: Run local SharePoint Online permission audits and produce readable reports.
skill.author: Aqualia

security_audit.summary: The skill is legitimate administrative automation, but it instructs agents to execute local PowerShell and Python commands with certificate-authenticated SharePoint access. Direct command execution findings are confirmed, while several Markdown inline-code detections are false positives. No prompt injection attempt or malicious data-exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: PowerShell and Python commands are run from skill instructions.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before each command, display the exact command, and validate all paths and arguments before execution.

remediation.issue: Module installation can fetch dependencies during setup.
remediation.suggestion: Pin required module versions, document trusted package sources, and ask users to approve installation before running Install-Modules.ps1.

remediation.issue: The workflow handles PFX credentials and sensitive SharePoint audit reports.
remediation.suggestion: Keep secrets in environment variables, redact sensitive values from logs, and store generated reports in access-controlled local directories.

content.value_statement: SharePoint permission reviews expose sensitive access paths but can be hard to collect consistently. This skill guides a local audit that produces readable reports.
actual_capabilities: Collects tenant ID, client ID, PFX path, internal domains, and site input before the audit.
Checks that PowerShell 7.4+, Python 3.10+, and PnP.PowerShell are available locally.
Runs the local module installation script and Python audit agent when the user approves.
Uses certificate authentication through the local PowerShell wrapper described by the skill.
Points users to generated HTML reports and warns that the reports contain sensitive data.
Defaults Sites.Selected permission guidance to Read unless the user authorizes Write.
limitations: Requires a local checkout that contains the referenced SharePoint audit agent scripts.
Requires valid Microsoft 365 app registration details and certificate authentication material.
Runs local shell commands and module installation, so it is not suitable for automatic execution.
Does not replace administrator approval, legal review, or formal compliance sign-off.

use_cases.title: Review Site Access
use_cases.description: Audit one SharePoint Online site and produce a local report for permission review.

use_cases.title: Investigate Exposure
use_cases.description: Collect permission evidence for sites that may expose internal or external users.

use_cases.title: Prepare Access Evidence
use_cases.description: Generate readable reports that support recurring access reviews and compliance discussions.

prompt_templates.title: Audit One Site
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through a local SharePoint audit for one site. Ask for every required value before running any command.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a single SharePoint site

prompt_templates.title: Check Prerequisites
prompt_templates.prompt: Confirm whether my local environment is ready for the SharePoint audit. Do not install modules until I approve.

prompt_templates.title: Run Batch Audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a batch SharePoint permission audit from my CSV input. Show the exact commands and wait for confirmation.
prompt_templates.scenario: Multiple site audit with controlled execution

prompt_templates.title: Review Audit Output
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me interpret the generated SharePoint audit report and identify access review items without exposing secrets.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of generated report findings

output_examples.input: Audit a SharePoint site after I provide tenant, client, certificate, domain, and site details.
output_examples.output: The assistant asks for missing inputs, confirms prerequisites, shows the local commands, and waits for approval before execution.

output_examples.input: The audit finished successfully and created a report folder.
output_examples.output: The assistant points to the generated HTML report and reminds the user that it contains sensitive access data.

output_examples.input: Review whether Write permission is needed for Sites.Selected.
output_examples.output: The assistant keeps Read as the default and asks for explicit authorization before using Write permission.

best_practices: Review every generated command before allowing the assistant to run it.
Store PFX passwords only in environment variables and avoid printing secret values.
Keep generated reports in restricted local folders because they contain sensitive permission data.
anti_patterns: Do not run the skill in an unattended agent session.
Do not paste certificate passwords or private keys into chat.
Do not grant Write permission unless the audit workflow truly requires it.

faq.question: Does this skill connect to SharePoint directly?
faq.answer: It guides local scripts that connect to SharePoint Online through certificate-based authentication.

faq.question: Can it run without PowerShell?
faq.answer: No. The skill requires local PowerShell, Python, and PnP.PowerShell tooling.

faq.question: Does it install anything?
faq.answer: It can run a local module installation script, so users should approve that step first.

faq.question: Is it safe for automatic execution?
faq.answer: No. It runs local commands and handles sensitive Microsoft 365 access data.

faq.question: What outputs does it produce?
faq.answer: The skill points users to generated HTML reports under the local runs directory.

faq.question: Does it use least privilege?
faq.answer: The skill instructs users to default Sites.Selected permission to Read unless Write is explicitly authorized.
